Explanation (mechanism): execution falls into case 3 because case 3 is the next labelled statement in source order and labels don't stop control. The output values are right but the stated reason is false.

Maths: with_break.c with n = 2 enters case 2 (line 9), prints two (line 10), and the break on line 11 ends the switch. Then done (line 18) runs. This matches the facts, and the line numbers in the justification are right.

Framing: scenes sc3, sc4 and sc5 have states s1, s2 and s3, which add the output lines two, three and done one at a time. The sentence makes no claim about C. The SPEC reference in the justification can't be checked from the job, but the claim doesn't depend on it.

Explanation: the sentence restates the last sentence of the stored 6.8.4.2p5 passage word for word in meaning. The programs have no default label.

Explanation: the switch body is a single statement (6.8.4 syntax, 6.8.4.2p4), and statements run in sequence (6.8p2), so once the body completes, the switch completes. The justification's line numbers (p1 line 16, p2 line 18) are right.

Framing, backed by the programs: with_break.c adds break on lines 8 and 11, case 3 already breaks (line 14), and case 4 is last, so no case's statements run into another case. The gcc-16 diagnostics are two warnings for fallthrough.c and none for with_break.c, as the justification says. The man passage says -Wextra enables -Wimplicit-fallthrough=3.

Media/diagnostics: the recorded gcc-16 output for fallthrough.c has fallthrough warnings at 7:9 and 9:9, and the output for with_break.c is empty. The man passage says -Wextra enables the warning. The claim is scoped to gcc-16 with -Wextra.

Maths and explanation: into_break.c differs from fallthrough.c only in case 3 (line 10), which holds just break; (line 11). With n = 2 it prints two, crosses the case 3 label, breaks, and prints done (line 15). This matches the facts.

Diagnostics: the recorded gcc-16 output for into_break.c has exactly one warning, at 7:9 with a note at case 2 on line 8, and nothing at line 9. The claim is scoped to into_break.c and gcc-16 with -Wextra.

Sources and caveats: the cited evidence, the clang diagnostics in lesson.json, is not in the job (the programs only carry gcc-16 diagnostics), so the claim can't be checked. The justification's claim that 'any clang warning would stop the capture' can't be checked either. The sentence also drops the version scope (Apple clang 21.0.0 in platform).
